title: Small house on posts, from Jim's pencil sketch

reasons.above_grade_mm: the sketch's '?' from grade to the floor; Jim's word gives it
reasons.section_mm: the sketch draws no post size; Jim's choice or a load check gives it

reasons.thickness_mm: the sketch draws no joist or deck; Jim's framing gives it

reasons.height_mm: reading: the south elevation's '12' as wall height, floor top to roof underside; 12 ft overall above grade is the other reading
reasons.thickness_mm: the sketch draws no stud or sheathing; Jim's framing gives it

reasons.north_eave_mm: reading: the hatched hangover on the south, 8 ft past the floor; centred, 5 ft each end, is the other reading
reasons.thickness_mm: the sketch draws no rafter or deck; Jim's framing gives it

reasons.glass_height_mm: Jim, 2026-10-17: one 8 ft by 8 ft window on the south wall, the top 4 ft lighting a sleeping loft and the lower 4 ft the living space
reasons.sill_height_mm: Jim: the first 4 ft of the south wall is a SIP panel below the window
reasons.window_width_mm: Jim: the window takes the 8 ft wall's whole width

reasons.u_value: assumed: typical double glazing, not chosen by Jim
reasons.solar_heat_gain_coefficient: assumed: typical double glazing, not chosen by Jim
reasons.sun_watt_per_square_metre: assumed clear-sky peak; the solver applies it to every side

reasons.mean_reflectance: assumed mid-grey interior; Jim's wall finish gives it
reasons.glass_transmittance: the BRE standard figure for double glazing as the Camden daylight reports quote it
reasons.sky_angle_degrees: assumed open sky; the site gives it

reasons.wall_r: assumed R-20 for a SIP wall (ft2 F h per BTU); the SIP thickness gives it
reasons.roof_r: assumed R-30; the roof build-up gives it
reasons.floor_r: assumed R-20; the floor build-up gives it

reasons.heating_degree_days_f: Traverse City's base-65F heating degree days: not found yet; NOAA climate normals for Cherry Capital Airport give it
reasons.glass_insolation_btu_per_ft2_season: winter sun on a vertical south face at the site: not found yet; NREL PVWatts at tilt 90 azimuth 180 gives it

reasons.fuel_btu_per_unit: Jim: one grown tree is about 20 million BTU, a cord of oak is 24 to 26 million by hobby sources
reasons.boiler_efficiency: assumed 70 percent; sources run 55 to 80 percent
